import.no_accounts: No bank accounts yet. Add one to import its transactions.
import.delete_account_confirm: Delete the account %s and its %d transactions?
import.import_hint: The file is read first and shown, so you can check it before anything is imported. Rows and receipts imported before are skipped.
import.imported: Imported %d new transactions; %s were imported before.
import.undo_confirm: Undo this import and delete its %d transactions?
import.err_csv: The file could not be read as CSV.
import.err_columns: Too few columns for this bank format.
import.err_date: Not a date in this bank format:
import.err_amount: Not an amount in this bank format:
import.delete_transaction_confirm: Delete %s (%s)? It comes back if a file with it is imported again.
plugin.import.about: Accounts per budget, with transactions imported from bank CSV exports and receipts from receipt exports, assigned to budget lines by rules.
import.unassigned_count: %d transactions in %d are not assigned to a budget line.
import.no_budget_year: The budget has no year %d, so its transactions cannot be assigned to lines yet.
import.remember_hint: Make a rule from the text, so transactions like it are assigned the same way
import.by_rule_hint: Assigned by a rule. Changing it here assigns it by hand.
import.assign_hint: Ignored transactions are not counted in the budget, e.g. transfers between your own accounts. With Remember ticked, a rule is made from the text without dates and used for the transactions not yet assigned.
import.rules_hint: A rule assigns every transaction whose text contains the rule's text, in any case. When several rules fit, the most specific wins. Rules only assign transactions that are not assigned; those assigned by hand are left alone.
import.rule_new: New rule, e.g. a loan number
import.rule_delete_confirm: Delete the rule %s? The %d transactions it assigned become unassigned.
import.no_rules: No rules yet. They are made when you assign transactions with Remember ticked, or here.
import.rule_err_duplicate: Two rules cannot have the same text.
import.rule_err_target: Choose a budget line for the new rule.
import.rule_err_empty: A rule needs some text besides *.
import.rules_tip_contains: The rule's text only has to be part of the transaction's text, in any case: pharmacy matches "Pharmacy Main Street 12" and "PHARMACY STATION".
import.rules_tip_star: * stands for any text: pharmacy*street matches "Pharmacy Main Street 12" and "Pharmacy High Street", but not "Pharmacy Station".
import.rules_tip_keep: Keep only the part that stays the same: pharmacy instead of "Card purchase Pharmacy Main Street 12".
import.compare_no_year: The budget has no years yet.
import.compare_unassigned: %d transactions in the period, %s in all, are not assigned to a line and not counted.
import.compare_hint: Actual is the sum of the transactions assigned to the line in the period; ignored ones are left out. The difference is green where the line did better than budgeted: less spent, or more earned.
import.compared_none: No months to compare: no transactions are imported for this year.
import.fill: Fill the budget from the bank…
import.fill_kept: %d amounts set by hand are kept. Choose Overwrite amounts to replace them too.
import.fill_hint: Each amount is saved like an edit on the budget page, with history, so it can be restored under Manage.
import.fill_nothing: Nothing to fill: the budget already has these amounts.
import.fill_untouched: Lines without transactions in a month, and linked lines, are not changed.
import.missing: %d budget lines have no transaction yet in the imported months, %s in all.
import.rule_test_note: Testing changes nothing. A rule only takes transactions that are not assigned by hand, and a more specific rule wins. At most 50 are shown, newest first.
import.missing_hint: A forgotten bill, a payment from another account, or a transaction not assigned yet.
import.rule_display_title: Shown in the transaction list instead of the bank's text. Matching still uses the bank's text.
import.split_hint: Give each part a budget line, or Ignore, and an amount. Amounts count in the transaction's direction, so a purchase of 1,000 split as 600 and 400 needs no minus; a minus counts the other way, e.g. a deposit refund. Leave one amount empty to give that part the rest.
import.split_undo_confirm: Undo the split? The transaction becomes whole and unassigned again.
import.split_err_line: Choose a budget line or Ignore for each part.
import.split_err_rest: Only one part can be left empty to take the rest.
import.split_err_sum: The parts add up to %s, but the transaction is %s.
import.default_line_hint: The account's transactions go to this line when no rule fits, e.g. all purchases on a food account.
import.by_default_hint: Assigned by the account's default line. Changing it here assigns it by hand.
import.by_receipt_hint: Split by the receipt's items, or ignored because a receipt covers it. Changing it here sets it by hand.
import.receipts_hint: Receipts imported before, or twice in the file, are skipped. A bank row a new receipt covers is ignored, so the purchase is not counted twice.
import.line_receipts_hint: Items count on the line their receipt split them to. Receipts split by hand are left out.
import.month_sum: %s in all, from %d purchases, %d of them with a receipt.
import.month_empty: Nothing is on the line this month.
import.search_count: %d purchases, newest first. The date opens the month.
import.search_more: The newest %d purchases. Search more precisely to see older ones.
import.search_none: No items on the line match “%s”.
